title: CYSTINOSIS, LATE-ONSET JUVENILE OR ADOLESCENT NEPHROPATHIC TYPE

relationships.phenotype: CYSTINOSIS, LATE-ONSET JUVENILE OR ADOLESCENT NEPHROPATHIC TYPE

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that late-onset juvenile or adolescent nephropathic cystinosis is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CTNS gene (606272) on chromosome 17p13.

checks.claim: Late-onset juvenile or adolescent nephropathic cystinosis is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CTNS gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease occurs due either to the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis or to homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation.
checks.explanation: Intermediate cystinosis is caused by compound heterozygous or homozygous CTNS mutations.

checks.claim: The CTNS gene is located on chromosome 17p13.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not give a chromosomal location.

paragraphs.text: Juvenile or adolescent nephropathic cystinosis is an autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder. Cystine builds up inside lysosomes because the lysosomal cystine transporter, cystinosin, does not work properly. It is an intermediate form of cystinosis, between the severe infantile nephropathic form and the benign adult nonnephropathic (ocular) form. Kidney disease begins later than in the infantile form and progresses more slowly to end-stage renal failure. Patients also have corneal cystine crystals.

checks.claim: Juvenile or adolescent nephropathic cystinosis is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease occurs due either to the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis or to homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation.
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance is implied by the biallelic genotypes but is not stated.

checks.claim: Juvenile or adolescent nephropathic cystinosis is a lysosomal storage disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: caused by a defect in the transport of cystine across the lysosomal membrane
checks.explanation: A lysosomal transport defect is described for the infantile form; the term 'lysosomal storage disorder' and its application to the juvenile form are not stated.

checks.claim: In juvenile nephropathic cystinosis, cystine accumulates inside lysosomes.
checks.evidence_quote: caused by a defect in the transport of cystine across the lysosomal membrane
checks.explanation: The abstract implies a lysosomal cystine transport defect but does not explicitly state lysosomal accumulation in the juvenile form.

checks.claim: In juvenile nephropathic cystinosis, lysosomal cystine accumulates because the lysosomal cystine transporter cystinosin is defective.
checks.evidence_quote: Structure predictions suggested that the gene product, cystinosin, is a novel integral lysosomal membrane protein.
checks.explanation: Cystinosin is described as a lysosomal membrane protein and the disease as a cystine transport defect; the abstract does not explicitly call cystinosin the transporter or link this to the juvenile form.

checks.claim: Juvenile nephropathic cystinosis is an intermediate form of cystinosis, between the severe infantile nephropathic form and the benign adult nonnephropathic (ocular) form.
checks.evidence_quote: Six patients with the intermediate form of cystinosis are described.
checks.explanation: The abstract uses the term 'intermediate form' but does not say it lies between the infantile and ocular forms.

checks.claim: In juvenile nephropathic cystinosis, kidney disease begins later than in infantile nephropathic cystinosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Late-onset cystinosis, a rarer form of the disorder, is characterized by onset of symptoms between 12 and 15 years of age.
checks.explanation: Later onset of symptoms is stated, but kidney disease is not specifically mentioned.

checks.claim: In juvenile nephropathic cystinosis, kidney disease progresses to end-stage renal failure more slowly than in infantile nephropathic cystinosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Renal failure in a sibship with late-onset cystinosis.
checks.explanation: The title confirms renal failure in late-onset cystinosis. It says nothing about the disease progressing more slowly than in the infantile form.

checks.claim: Patients with juvenile nephropathic cystinosis have corneal cystine crystals.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not mention corneal crystals.

paragraphs.text: Kidney involvement in the late-onset form usually becomes apparent in late childhood or adolescence. It often presents with proteinuria, which can reach the nephrotic range, rather than the full renal Fanconi syndrome seen in infants. Renal function declines more slowly than in the infantile form, but end-stage renal disease eventually develops. Cystine crystals are found in the cornea and other tissues, and growth is less affected than in infantile cystinosis.

checks.claim: Kidney involvement in late-onset nephropathic cystinosis usually becomes apparent in late childhood or adolescence.
checks.evidence_quote: Late-onset cystinosis, a rarer form of the disorder, is characterized by onset of symptoms between 12 and 15 years of age.
checks.explanation: Onset in adolescence is stated, but kidney involvement specifically is not.

checks.claim: Kidney involvement in late-onset nephropathic cystinosis often presents with proteinuria rather than the full renal Fanconi syndrome seen in infantile cystinosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not mention proteinuria or Fanconi syndrome.

checks.claim: Proteinuria in late-onset nephropathic cystinosis can reach the nephrotic range.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not mention nephrotic-range proteinuria.

checks.claim: In late-onset nephropathic cystinosis, renal function declines more slowly than in infantile nephropathic cystinosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not mention how fast renal function declines.

checks.claim: Patients with late-onset nephropathic cystinosis eventually develop end-stage renal disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Renal failure in a sibship with late-onset cystinosis.
checks.explanation: The title reports renal failure in one sibship with late-onset cystinosis. It does not establish that end-stage renal disease develops in patients generally.

checks.claim: In late-onset nephropathic cystinosis, cystine crystals are found in the cornea and other tissues.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not mention crystals.

checks.claim: Growth is less affected in late-onset nephropathic cystinosis than in infantile cystinosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not mention growth.

paragraphs.text: Free cystine levels in leukocytes are raised, typically to intermediate values. Patients' cells have reduced carrier-mediated transport of cystine out of lysosomes. Measuring leukocyte cystine is the standard diagnostic test, as in the other forms of cystinosis.

checks.claim: In juvenile nephropathic cystinosis, free cystine levels in leukocytes are elevated, typically to intermediate values.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not report leukocyte cystine levels.

checks.claim: Cells from patients with juvenile nephropathic cystinosis have reduced carrier-mediated transport of cystine out of lysosomes.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract mentions 'partial phenotypic correction' of fibroblasts but does not describe a transport defect.

checks.claim: Measurement of leukocyte cystine is the standard diagnostic test for juvenile nephropathic cystinosis, as in the other forms of cystinosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss diagnostic testing.

paragraphs.text: Juvenile nephropathic cystinosis is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. It is allelic to infantile nephropathic cystinosis and to adult nonnephropathic (ocular) cystinosis.

checks.claim: Juvenile nephropathic cystinosis is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease occurs due either to the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis or to homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation.
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance is implied by the biallelic mutations but is not stated.

checks.claim: Juvenile nephropathic cystinosis is allelic to infantile nephropathic cystinosis.
checks.evidence_quote: the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis
checks.explanation: Intermediate cystinosis shares CTNS alleles with nephropathic cystinosis.

checks.claim: Juvenile nephropathic cystinosis is allelic to adult nonnephropathic (ocular) cystinosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not mention ocular or adult cystinosis.

paragraphs.text: Thoene et al. (1999) and Attard et al. (1999) identified mutations in the CTNS gene in patients with intermediate (juvenile) cystinosis. These patients usually had at least one milder allele, such as a missense or splice mutation that leaves some cystinosin function. This contrasts with infantile nephropathic cystinosis, in which both alleles are typically severe, for example the common 57-kb deletion found in patients of northern European ancestry.

checks.claim: Thoene et al. (1999) identified mutations in the CTNS gene in patients with intermediate (juvenile) cystinosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Six patients with the intermediate form of cystinosis are described. Two have new mutations not previously described.
checks.explanation: The title and abstract report CTNS mutations in intermediate cystinosis.

checks.claim: Attard et al. (1999) identified mutations in the CTNS gene in patients with intermediate (juvenile) cystinosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations found in two late-onset patients affect functionally unimportant regions of cystinosin, which accounts for their milder phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports CTNS mutations in late-onset patients.

checks.claim: Patients with intermediate (juvenile) cystinosis usually had at least one milder CTNS allele, such as a missense or splice mutation that leaves some residual cystinosin function.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease occurs due either to the combination of one mild mutation and one which is known to cause nephropathic cystinosis or to homozygosity for a predicted mild mutation.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports at least one mild allele but does not name missense or splice mutation types or residual function.

checks.claim: In infantile nephropathic cystinosis, both CTNS alleles are typically severe.
checks.evidence_quote: 12 have two severely truncating mutations, which is consistent with a loss of functional protein, and 13 have missense or in-frame deletions, which would result in disruption of transmembrane domains and loss of protein function.
checks.explanation: Every infantile patient had mutations predicted to cause loss of function.

checks.claim: A common 57-kb deletion in CTNS is a severe allele found in patients with infantile nephropathic cystinosis of northern European ancestry.
checks.evidence_quote: including a common, approximately 65 kb deletion which encompasses exons 1-10
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract gives the common deletion as about 65 kb, not 57 kb, and does not mention northern European ancestry.

paragraphs.text: Attard et al. (1999) reported that the severity of cystinosis depended on the CTNS genotype. In their study, patients with the infantile form tended to have 2 severe alleles, while those with the juvenile and ocular forms carried at least one mild allele.

checks.claim: Attard et al. (1999) reported that the severity of cystinosis depended on the CTNS genotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Severity of phenotype in cystinosis varies with mutations in the CTNS gene: predicted effect on the model of cystinosin.
checks.explanation: The title states that severity varies with the CTNS mutation.

checks.claim: In the study by Attard et al. (1999), patients with infantile cystinosis tended to have 2 severe CTNS alleles.
checks.evidence_quote: Out of 25 patients with infantile nephropathic cystinosis, 12 have two severely truncating mutations
checks.explanation: Only 12 of 25 had two truncating alleles; the other 13 had missense or in-frame deletions, described as still causing loss of function.

checks.claim: In the study by Attard et al. (1999), patients with juvenile and ocular cystinosis carried at least one mild CTNS allele.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations found in two late-onset patients affect functionally unimportant regions of cystinosin, which accounts for their milder phenotype.
checks.explanation: Milder mutations are reported in late-onset patients; ocular cystinosis patients are not mentioned in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: As in the infantile form, oral cysteamine lowers the cystine content of cells, and cysteamine eye drops are used to treat the corneal crystals.

checks.claim: In juvenile nephropathic cystinosis, as in the infantile form, oral cysteamine lowers cellular cystine content.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not mention cysteamine; it reports only correction of fibroblasts by cDNA transfection.

checks.claim: In juvenile nephropathic cystinosis, as in the infantile form, cysteamine eye drops are used to treat corneal cystine crystals.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 6 cited papers. The abstract does not mention cysteamine eye drops.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Slowly progressive renal failure in adolescence
Renal Fanconi syndrome (milder than infantile form)
